Manchester University Press (MUP) is situated in the heart of one of the most vibrant universities and cities in the UK. Founded in 1904, we're the third largest university press in England, and our distinctive brand is known globally for excellent research in the Humanities and Social Sciences from leading names and up-and-coming scholars around the World. We currently publish over 170 books each year, as well as seven journals.

result.title: The Ten Best Short Films on Netflix
result.text:
Set over three different time periods – past, present and future – the three individual chapters of The House not only tell the story of this unusual dwelling, but they also work as an eye-catching showcasing for the filmmakers involved. Independent stop-motion isn't something that's given a pedestal like this very often, but with this and Robin Robin now on Netflix, fingers crossed for more in the future

WATCH ON NETFLIX

***

2. Love, Death + Robots

Dir: Various

With Blur Studio co-founder Tim Miller (Deadpool) as creator and David Fincher as an Executive Producer, this high-profile animated anthology of science fiction short films is far too significant to leave off any list of short films on Netflix. Though the quality of the shorts varies throughout Volume 1 and the series received criticism for its representation of women, the highs in this 18 film collection are stunningly high, and, importantly, as an exciting and popular anthology for Netflix, the series is proving to be an important milestone for mature-themed animation in television.

Volume 2 was released in May 2021 and you can check out our guide to the eight standalone shorts – featuring giants, robotic servants and Michael B. Jordan – and their directors for more information.

Volume 3 was then released in May the following year (2022) and saw David Fincher direct his first episode of the series he's executive produced since its inception and saw more recognisable names from short film (Patrick Osborne, Alberto Mielgo) join its ranks. Again, you can check our in-depth guide to discover more about the individual episodes.

result.title: Animation Directors and Films: Everything you need to know
result.text:
Beavis and Butt-Head, King of the Hill, The Goode Family, Silicon Valley, Mike Judge Presents: Tales from the Tour Bus, among others are some of his finest works.

He bagged a Primetime Emmy Award and two Annie Awards for King of the Hill as well as two Critics' Choice Television Awards and Satellite Awards for his work as an animation director in Silicon Valley.

Rob Letterman: Having co-directed the iconic Hollywood animated film Shark Tale and bagged an Annie Award nomination for Writing in a Feature Production, Rob Letterman is one of the most popular animation directors.

He is best known for directing popular animated films like Monsters vs. Aliens, Gulliver's Travels, Goosebumps, Detective Pikachu, among others. He is also the director of Pokémon Detective Pikachu, the second-highest-grossing video game film adaptation.

Marjane Satrapi: The Iranian artist and animator who started her career through popular and critically acclaimed graphic novels Persepolis and The Sigh is one of the most renowned animation directors.

She bagged the Academy nomination for Best Animated Film for her debut animated film Persepolis which was based on her novel of the same name and later won millions of hearts with her excellent work in films like Chicken with Plums, The Voices, Radioactive, among others.

Phil Lord And Christopher Miller: The famous American filmmaking duo is known for their path breaking work in the adult animated sitcom Clone High. They also directed and wrote the famous Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs which is an American computer-animated science-fiction comedy film produced by Sony Pictures Animation.

2014's The Lego Movie is another great animated film directed by this duo that makes them the best animation directors across the globe. They also won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature as producers of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse.
